requirement:
During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST
display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.preparation` says: "During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage." Every clause describes behavior a user can observe. They cover when the display appears (during preparation, on an enabled terminal), that it updates, and that it names the current stage. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface.

I tested the candidate structural obligations against alternatives:
- A spinner or progress bar could come from a hand-written loop, a progress crate, or a background thread. Each gives the same observable display, so the mechanism is discretionary.
- Stage names could be passed as a parameter, kept in shared state, or emitted by an event callback. All still satisfy "identify the current preparation stage", so the plumbing is discretionary.
- The terminal gating (stderr interactive, `TERM` not `dumb`) is defined in the cited `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`. That text is context here and is not a structural obligation of the subject.

No implementation roots were supplied, and none are needed. The obligations are behavioral and belong to test evidence.

behavioral: The requirement has two obligations. On an enabled terminal, preparation must show updating activity. It must also identify the current preparation stage. The `terminal` requirement is cited as context only. Tests cover its enablement and clearing, and I did not reassess them.

**Stage identification.**
- `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared]` creates the preparation display on a recording terminal. It asserts that the "Recording inputs" text appears. It then calls `stage("Capturing coverage maps")` and asserts that the new stage text appears, so a stage change is shown.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy]` runs the real binary on a PTY with `TERM=xterm`. It asserts that stderr contains "Preparing coverage: recording inputs" and "Preparing coverage: capturing maps".
- Those are the two preparation stages. I found them in `Progress::preparation` and `runner::run`, which calls `progress.stage("Preparing coverage: capturing maps")`.
- The same PTY test runs with `TERM=dumb`. It asserts that there are no control sequences and no "Converting coverage" text. That is consistent with display being limited to enabled terminals.

**Updating activity.**
- `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[preparation_activity_keeps_updating_without_a_stage_change]` creates a preparation display with no stage change. It polls the recorded frames until at least two distinct frames contain "Recording inputs". It asserts that every such frame carries an elapsed-time marker. A static display would fail this test.
- The PTY test also asserts that in-place updating escape sequences are present and that elapsed-time text ("[00:") appears.

**Failure path.** The PTY test also covers preparation failing. It asserts that the stage is shown and then cleared before the diagnostic. Clearing belongs to the `terminal` requirement, so this is only extra evidence.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there are no marking gaps.

text: During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under
display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage.
Habeas coverage progress MUST be displayed when stderr is an interactive
terminal and `TERM` is not `dumb`. `NO_COLOR` MUST disable color without
disabling progress. When stderr is redirected or `TERM=dumb`, Habeas coverage
progress MUST NOT emit animation or terminal control sequences.
Temporary progress displays MUST be cleared when their stage ends, including
empty work and early collection failures. Final diagnostics and the coverage
artifact location MUST remain readable. Progress reporting MUST NOT change
coverage results, retained profiles, or command exit status.
